title: How Sam Bankman-Fried Lost Out on a $35 Billion Jackpot From Anthropic
summary: The founder of the collapsed FTX crypto exchange, who is serving prison time for fraud, would have made a windfall from a $500 million investment in Anthropic.

Sam Bankman-Fried, the convicted cryptocurrency fraudster, lives in a 30-person unit at the federal prison in Lompoc, Calif., a barbed-wire compound about a million miles away from his former life as a technology billionaire in the Bahamas.


For the most part, Mr. Bankman-Fried, 34, tries not to think about all the “could-have-beens,” he said on a recent call. But one has become difficult to ignore.


In late 2021, the heyday of his FTX crypto exchange, Mr. Bankman-Fried[spent](https://restructuring.ra.kroll.com/ftx/Home-DownloadPDF?id1=MzA1NzAzMA==&id2=-1) $500 million on a 13.5 percent stake in a little-known artificial intelligence start-up called Anthropic. This week, Anthropic is set for an initial public offering that is[expected](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/10/technology/anthropic-ipo-valuation-share-price.html) to value the company at $1.4 trillion, potentially one of the largest Wall Street debuts in history.


At that valuation, Mr. Bankman-Fried’s investment, diluted over several years, would now be worth an eye-watering $35 billion — about the size of FTX’s entire business at its peak.


But the shares are gone. They were tied up in bankruptcy court until 2024, when executives overseeing the scattered remains of FTX[sold](https://restructuring.ra.kroll.com/ftx/Home-DownloadPDF?id1=MzExNDkzMg==&id2=-1)[the](https://restructuring.ra.kroll.com/ftx/Home-DownloadPDF?id1=MzA4OTczNA==&id2=-1) Anthropic stake for $1.34 billion — a tiny fraction of its current value.


For Anthropic, the fate of those shares is an odd quirk of history. For Mr. Bankman-Fried, it’s a source of extreme frustration and resentment. Even after a fraud conviction, a[failed appeal](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/06/12/sam-bankman-frieds-conviction-upheld-by-appeals-court-00960434) and a succession of public humiliations, he is still trying to prove his innocence, arguing that FTX had sufficient resources to avoid bankruptcy.
